sources.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, extended and corrected Summer 2016 lecture notes, arXiv:1311.2717v2
sources.locator: Complete author-hosted 157-page PDF. Read the full relevant KMS section §3.4, printed pp. 74–78 (PDF pages 74–78): Definition 3.4.4, Proposition 3.4.5, finite Gibbs/KMS and uniqueness discussion, and Corollary 3.4.9. The complete PDF was previously retrieved into research/physics-remaining-80-2026-10-17-batch-39-sources/raw/ and its exact bytes/hash were re-inspected; unrelated chapters were not claimed as read.

contents.name: §3.4, Definition 3.4.4, printed p. 74: physical-time KMS strip and reversed upper boundary
contents.support: The notes use the closed strip of width ħβ and the same lower/upper correlation order. They later set ħ=1; this item retains physical seconds explicitly.

contents.name: §3.4, finite Gibbs calculation and matrix-unit uniqueness discussion, printed pp. 76–77
contents.support: The source gives the finite Gibbs strip identity and sketches uniqueness through matrix units. The item supplies the full finite-dimensional derivation, including degeneracies and the one-dimensional case.

contents.name: §3.4, Corollary 3.4.9 and finite Gibbs limit discussion, printed pp. 77–78
contents.support: The source motivates finite-volume Gibbs limits as a route to KMS states; this local lemma supplies the explicit trace extension, state compactness, derivative bound, and closed-strip convergence under the stated finite-range assumptions.

contents.name: §3.4, Corollary 3.4.9: existence of infinite spin KMS states, printed pp. 77–78
contents.support: The source states the existence conclusion for its strictly local bounded interaction framework. The item proves the exact local-pair limit and all-observable norm extension under its explicit conditional finite-matrix interfaces.

contents.name: §3.4, finite Gibbs boundary example, printed pp. 76–77
contents.support: The two-level example is a direct finite-matrix specialization of the source Gibbs/KMS calculation and checks the physical-time exponential sign explicitly.

sources.title: David Ruelle, Topics in Quantum Statistical Mechanics and Operator Algebras, complete author-hosted lecture notes, arXiv:math-ph/0107009v1
sources.locator: Complete 36-page author-hosted PDF, dated 11 July 2001. Read Chapter 1 §7, printed pp. 12–13, and Chapter 2 §6, printed pp. 23–24, including the KMS strip theorem, invariance and correlation bound, local Gibbs state, and Gibbs/KMS discussion. The source uses its own rescaled time convention; no ħ=1 convention is silently transferred to the authored statements.

contents.name: Chapter 1 §7, KMS condition theorem, printed pp. 12–13: analytic strip boundary identity, invariance and norm bound
contents.support: The notes state that the KMS condition implies invariance and the correlation norm bound. This item supplies the full periodic-gluing, Morera, and Liouville proof rather than taking the consequence on authority.

contents.name: Chapter 1 §7, analytic-strip KMS definition, printed p. 12
contents.support: The abstract strip convention agrees after the source’s stated time rescaling and ħ=1 convention; the authored definition fixes βħ seconds and states boundedness explicitly.

contents.name: Chapter 2 §6, local Gibbs states and Gibbs/KMS discussion, printed pp. 23–24
contents.support: The source constructs local Gibbs states and records that limit points are KMS under an exponentially summable interaction condition. The item gives the finite-range specialization with its full conditional compactness and strip-limit argument.

contents.name: Chapter 2 §6, finite local Gibbs state and KMS/Gibbs equivalence, printed pp. 23–24
contents.support: The source states the finite local Gibbs/KMS characterization with its operator-algebraic hypotheses. The item proves the two directions explicitly using finite matrix units and the bounded-strip uniqueness lemma.

contents.name: Chapter 1 §7, KMS strip correlation bound, printed p. 12
contents.support: The source records the uniform correlation bound for the KMS strip condition. The item proves the required closed-strip estimate and lower-edge uniqueness directly from the imported Hadamard three-lines theorem.

contents.name: Chapter 1 §7, finite-time Gibbs/KMS convention, printed pp. 12–13
contents.support: The source gives the finite Gibbs/KMS convention in a rescaled time variable. The example checks the same boundary relation with explicit SI units and physical time.
